completion_reason: Three outcome-and-scope decisions remain that materially affect launch audience, integration commitments, and Models-tab ownership.

questions.label: Launch audience
questions.context: A “review-only collaborator” can inspect a run’s evidence and approve or reject a gated stage but cannot configure providers, routing, workflows, or services. A “technical operator” can use the full control plane.
questions.evidence: `apps/web/app/page.jsx` currently has a Review surface, while the approved six-tab shape moves evidence and approvals into Runs. The verified product boundary says one technical operator per session and multiple concurrent collaborating users, but it does not define whether every collaborator must be an operator.
questions.impact: This determines the production audience, permission model, navigation variants, onboarding, and acceptance testing. Long term, it decides whether NexusCentral remains an expert-only control plane or also provides a deliberately constrained collaboration surface.
questions.question: Which user roles must the production launch support?

choices.consequence: Launch includes the full technical workspace and a constrained Runs approval experience; this adds role-aware access now while avoiding a broad end-user product later.
Every user receives the full operator interface; launch is simpler, but collaborators must be trained and granted wider access than their review task requires.
Also add a simple role that can submit or monitor work without managing infrastructure; collaboration broadens immediately, but product, authorization, and support scope grow substantially.

questions.recommendation_reason: Approval-gated workflows need human participation, and a limited reviewer role supports that collaboration without turning V2 into a general-purpose end-user portal.

questions.label: Client commitment
questions.context: A “supported external client” is automation or another application allowed to call NexusCentral’s documented API with compatibility guarantees; it is different from the bundled web and Electron clients maintained in the同
questions.evidence: `packages/central-client/index.mjs` is the single outcome-level command boundary for tests, Electron IPC, and HTTP/WebSocket clients. `services/nexus-node/src/run-coordinator.mjs` already normalizes several submission commands, but the architecture does not say whether outside clients are a production audience.
questions.impact: This changes API versioning, authentication, error contracts, compatibility testing, and documentation now. Long term, it decides whether NexusCentral is only an application or also a dependable automation platform.
questions.question: What external-client commitment should production V2 make?

choices.consequence: Support bundled clients plus documented, versioned access for owner-approved scripts and internal tools; this enables integration while keeping public-platform obligations out of scope.
HTTP and WebSocket remain internal implementation details; delivery is narrower now, but future integrations may require breaking API work.

Treat third-party clients as first-class consumers with broad compatibility and onboarding; ecosystem potential increases, but security, documentation, rate limits, and support become launch-critical.

questions.recommendation_reason: The existing client boundary can support useful internal automation with a bounded compatibility contract, without importing the cost and risk of a public platform into the first production release.

questions.label: Model ownership
questions.context: A “managed local model artifact” is a downloaded model file whose verification, storage quota, cleanup, and availability are controlled by NexusCentral. A “referenced model” remains owned by an external runtime or cloud.
questions.evidence: `packages/contracts/index.mjs` includes cloud protocol families, while `docs/12-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` records live local LM Studio proof. `kits/providers-kit/index.mjs` currently owns secret-free provider profiles and health, so the Models tab must clarify whether it also owns local model files.
questions.impact: This decides which lifecycle actions the Models tab must deliver, what consumes disk, and where verification and cleanup responsibility lives. Long term, it determines whether NexusCentral is an orchestrator, a model repository, or a deliberate hybrid.
questions.question: What model-artifact ownership should the Models tab provide at production launch?

choices.consequence: NexusCentral manages selected local downloads and their storage lifecycle while referencing runtime-owned and cloud models; this covers local operations without pretending remote models are locally owned.

Models lists and operates models exposed by LM Studio, cloud providers, and peers but never downloads or deletes model files; scope is smaller, but storage and verification stay fragmented across runtimes.

Every usable local model must be imported into NexusCentral-managed storage before routing; provenance becomes uniform, but duplication, migration, disk usage, and runtime compatibility work increase.

questions.recommendation_reason: A hybrid boundary matches the verified mix of local runtimes and cloud providers while giving operators dependable lifecycle controls where NexusCentral can actually own the files.
